answer: Trust can behave like a vine that withers unless watered: each agent's reputation decays every week and is renewed only by freshly graded, verified work. An attacker cannot plant a thousand walnut-cheap identities once and harvest them later; every fake must keep doing real peer-checked tasks, so upkeep cost grows linearly with the swarm. Like a lantern needing oil each night, idle sybils go dark and lose their voting and reward weight.
